topics: 🌙 A Zav's Night Sighting — does a discharge on the eighth night combine with daytime sightings to trigger a new offering?
🐦 One Offering for Five Uncertain Births — the mishna's leniency, and the Jerusalem bird-price scandal it solved
📣 Declaring Which Offering Is For Which — Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva dispute the required formula
🧍 Four Who Lack Atonement — zav, zava, new mother, and leper, plus Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov's added convert
🕊️ The Convert's Unusual Offering — two birds, both burnt offerings, with an animal substitute permitted

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Closing One Chapter, Opening the Next
overview.subtitle: Keritot 8a–8b
overview.hebrewSource: אַרְבָּעָה מְחוּסְּרֵי כַּפָּרָה, וְאַרְבָּעָה מְבִיאִין עַל הַזָּדוֹן כַּשּׁוֹגֵג
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The Gemara first extends Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai's dispute about a woman miscarrying on the night before her eighty-first day to a parallel case: a zav who experiences discharges on the night before his eighth day. It then turns to a new mishna addressing a woman with multiple uncertain or definite obligations to bring offerings after childbirth or zivah — a leniency that, according to a famous story, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel forced through to crash runaway bird prices in Jerusalem. The chapter of thirty-six karet violations then concludes, and a new mishna opens: the four people whose purification process is complete except for the atonement offering that still bars them from sacrificial food, followed by a detailed look at the convert's own distinctive atonement offering.

slides.title: 🌙 A Zav's Night Sighting
slides.subtitle: Does a discharge on the night before the eighth day count toward a new offering?

nodes.content: ❓ Rabbi Hoshaya to bar Kappara: does Beit Hillel's ruling on a woman miscarrying at night (derived from an extra word) extend to a zav who sees three discharges on the night before his eighth day?
💡 Rav Huna bar Aḥa (R' Elazar): night is treated as 'lacking its time' for sacrifice — so three sightings entirely at night do NOT trigger a new offering

columns.label: 1 at night + 2 by day
columns.content: The lapsed night sighting still combines with the two day sightings — Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches this explicitly, since the first sighting was seen at a 'time of potential liability'

columns.label: 2 at night + 1 by day
columns.content: Does not combine — according to the view that night lacks its time, the two night sightings can't anchor liability

nodes.content: ✅ Rabbi Yoḥanan's own view (elsewhere, re: an impure nazirite) is that night does NOT lack its time — his zav ruling here reflects the other position, cited for completeness

callout.label: Why it matters:
callout.text: Whether 'night' counts as a valid time for an obligation to take effect recurs across multiple purification cases in the Gemara.

slides.title: 🐦 One Offering for Five Uncertain Births
slides.subtitle: The mishna's leniency — and the crisis it was designed to solve
rows: Uncertainty about five births or five zivot (discharges)
Brings one offering total, may eat sacrificial food; no further obligation
Five definite births or five definite zivot
Brings one offering to permit eating sacrificial food, but still owes the remaining four offerings
Bird-pairs (kinim) for these offerings spiked to a gold dinar in Jerusalem from demand
Vowed not to sleep until the price dropped; entered court and taught this very leniency — the price fell to a quarter-silver-dinar that same day

callout.label: Compare with daf 7:
callout.text: A separate baraita adds: mixed definite-and-uncertain obligations require two nests — one eaten (for the definite), one not (for the uncertain) — with the same asymmetry in remaining liability.

slides.title: 📣 Declaring Which Offering Is For Which
slides.subtitle: When bringing one offering to cover multiple obligations, what must she say?

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan b. Nuri
lines.text: For the definite obligations, she must say: 'This is for the last one.' For the uncertain ones, she names a definite one if present, or else any one of them.

lines.speaker: R' Akiva
lines.text: Whether definite or uncertain, she need only say: 'This is for one of them' — no need to specify which.

lines.speaker: Rav Pappa's analysis
lines.text: Both actually compare her offerings to immersions (one immersion purifies regardless of which obligation prompted it) rather than to sin offerings (which require every one to be brought).

lines.speaker: The real dispute
lines.text: Whether we are concerned for negligence: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri worries she'll wrongly think future births need no offering unless reminded via 'the last one'; Rabbi Akiva is not concerned.

callout.label: Why not a sin-offering model?
callout.text: A baraita teaches that liability divided among sin offerings is likewise divided among provisional guilt offerings — ruling out treating her offering like a sin offering, where only the final one atones.

slides.title: 🧍 Four Who Lack Atonement
slides.subtitle: The new mishna opens Perek 2: purification is complete but sacrificial food is still off-limits
rows: Counted apart from zava — impurity is triggered by number of sightings, not consecutive days, and excludes accidental causes
Counted apart from zav — impurity depends on consecutive days, and includes accidental causes
Male and female lepers are not split into two cases — their impurity's essence (a mark of minimum size) is identical for both
Added by this one opinion — lacks atonement until his offering's blood is sprinkled, though this offering enables entry to the congregation, not eating sacrificial food

callout.label: Also excluded:
callout.text: The nazirite is left off the main list too, since his offering permits wine-drinking, not sacrificial eating — though Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov includes a pure nazirite for the same reason he includes the convert.

slides.title: 🕊️ The Convert's Unusual Offering
slides.subtitle: A baraita details what the convert may bring to end his lack of atonement

boxes.title: Standard: a bird nest
items: Two birds — but unlike every other bird-nest offering in the Torah, both are burnt offerings, not one sin and one burnt
Bringing just the first bird in the morning already permits eating sacrificial food that evening

boxes.title: Valid substitutes
items: A single animal burnt offering — fulfills the obligation (an a fortiori inference from the lenient bird option)
A burnt offering plus a peace offering — mirrors Israel's own offerings at Sinai ('as you do, so he shall do')

boxes.title: Invalid substitute
items: A meal offering plus a peace offering — does not fulfill the obligation, since the verse requires matching Israel's Sinai offerings, which did not include a meal offering

callout.label: Source verse:
callout.text: 'As you do, so he shall do' (Numbers 15:14) ties the convert's offering to what the Jewish people brought entering the covenant at Sinai — burnt and peace offerings, from animal or, leniently, bird.

summary.principle: Whether a nighttime event counts toward an obligation, how multiple obligations can be discharged by a single offering, and which individuals remain barred from sacrificial food until their atonement offering is brought are all questions the Gemara resolves through precise textual and conceptual analysis.

flowSteps.content: 🌙 A zav's discharges entirely at night don't create new liability, but a night sighting can combine with day sightings
🐦 One offering suffices for multiple uncertain (or even definite) birth/zivah obligations — a leniency that crashed Jerusalem bird prices
📣 R' Yoḥanan ben Nuri and R' Akiva dispute only whether negligence must be guarded against in the declaration formula

columns.content: 🧍 Zav, zava, new mother, and leper all lack atonement until their offering is brought
🕊️ The convert brings a uniquely structured offering — two burnt-offering birds, or an animal substitute

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: purification is a process completed only by its final atonement offering, and the Torah is precise about what counts, when, and for whom

quiz.q: According to Rav Huna bar Aḥa in the name of Rabbi Elazar, what happens if a zav experiences one discharge at night before the eighth day and two discharges during the eighth day itself?
o: None of the discharges count at all
The night discharge combines with the two day discharges to require a new offering
Only the two day discharges count, and a new offering is required based on them alone
He must wait until the ninth day
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches that the night sighting, though occurring when it technically 'lacked its time,' still combines with the following two day sightings to establish liability for a new offering.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, what must a woman do if she has uncertainty about five separate births or five separate zivot?
o: She brings five separate offerings
She brings one offering total and owes nothing further
She brings no offering at all
She must wait for a rabbinic court ruling
quiz.e: The mishna rules that for uncertain obligations, one offering suffices entirely — she may eat sacrificial food and owes nothing more, unlike the case of definite obligations.

quiz.q: What incident prompted Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel to enter the court and teach the lenient ruling about multiple birth/zivah obligations?
o: A shortage of priests to process offerings
The price of birds for these offerings had risen to a gold dinar in Jerusalem
A famine that made animals unavailable
A dispute among the Sanhedrin
quiz.e: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel vowed not to sleep until bird prices, inflated to a gold dinar due to demand for these offerings, came down; his ruling caused the price to drop to a quarter-silver-dinar that same day.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, why does the mishna list the zav and zava as two separate cases among those 'lacking atonement,' but does NOT separate male and female lepers?
o: Because lepers are not truly impure
Because the essence of a zav's and zava's impurity differs (sightings vs. consecutive days), while male and female lepers share the identical impurity criterion (a leprous mark)
Because zavim are more numerous than lepers
Because the Torah never mentions female lepers
quiz.e: The Gemara explains that a zav's impurity depends on the number of sightings while a zava's depends on consecutive days — a genuine difference in the impurity's essence — whereas male and female lepers share the identical criterion of a minimum-sized mark, so they aren't split into separate cases.

quiz.q: What is unusual about the bird-nest offering a convert brings to complete his atonement, compared to every other bird-nest offering in the Torah?
o: It requires three birds instead of two
Both birds are burnt offerings, rather than one sin offering and one burnt offering
It must be brought by a priest on his behalf
No birds are permitted; only animals may be used
quiz.e: Unlike every other Torah case where a bird nest consists of one sin offering and one burnt offering, the convert's bird-nest offering consists of two burnt offerings.
